Contributing to WeGrowHealthR

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for helping to improve the package.

Reporting a problem

Open an issue at https://github.com/nhanhocu/WeGrowHealthR/issues with the bug report template. A good report has a short description, the full error message, a minimal example that runs on bundled or simulated data (for example wgh_simulate(2000, seed = 1)), and the output of sessionInfo() and wgh_parallel_info().

Never post real individual-level child data in an issue, even a few rows. Reproduce the problem on simulated data instead, or describe the structure of your data (column names, types, number of rows and children).

Suggesting a feature

Open an issue with the feature request template. Say which analysis it supports and which published method or book chapter it follows.

Changing the code

  1. Fork the repository and create a branch.
  2. Follow the existing style: exported functions start with wgh_, use .need() for suggested packages, .wgh_map() for anything that should run in parallel, and .try() so that failed models are recorded in the model status rather than stopping a flow.
  3. Add or update tests in tests/testthat/. Numerical results should be checked against an independent reference (published values, a closed form or another package) where one exists.
  4. Run devtools::document(), devtools::test() and R CMD check --as-cran before opening a pull request.
  5. Add a line to NEWS.md.

Vignettes

Eight vignettes are precomputed because their models take several minutes. Edit the .Rmd.orig file in vignettes/, never the knitted .Rmd, and then run Rscript precompute.R inside vignettes/. The two light vignettes (getting-started and simulated-data) are built in the normal way.

Code of conduct

Please note that this project is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By taking part you agree to abide by its terms.
